identity.name: Zhang Chu
identity.wikipedia: Chen Sheng and Wu Guang uprising

predecessors.note: Chen County under the Qin; Cliopatria's Qin Dynasty row runs -218..-209 (ea-02-a).

successors.note: After Zhang Han's counter-attacks (Chen Sheng page) the rebel Chu territory fell back to the Qin or to the break-away rebel kings; the pages name no heir of Chen County.

capitals.name: Chen (Huaiyang)
capitals.note: 'setting his capital at Chen County (in present-day Huaiyang, Henan)'; coordinates approximate.

rulers.name: Chen Sheng
rulers.title: King of Rising Chu (張楚王)
rulers.note: assassinated by his guard Zhuang Jia c. January 208 BC

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, -209..-208; no Cliopatria row (Qin Dynasty -218..-209 and Western Chu from -208). Chen Sheng 'setting his capital at Chen County (in present-day Huaiyang, Henan)'; the Chen Sheng and Wu Guang page names no commandery the rebels held, only that he 'could not firmly hold conquered territories'. A 70 km circle at Zhoukou stands for Chen County.

ledger.note: 209 BC: Chen Sheng is King of Rising Chu. The uprising began in the 7th month (9 Aug to 7 Sep 209 BC); Chen 'declared himself King of Rising Chu' 'only months after the start of his rebellion' (no month), with his capital at Chen County.

208 BC: Zhang Chu is lost. Chen Sheng was 'assassinated by his guard Zhuang Jia in c. January 208 BC' (4 Jan to 1 Feb); Qin forces 'regrouped under general Zhang Han'; Wu Chen, Zhou Fu and the generals who killed Wu Guang broke away. The pages name no holder of Chen County after the death; entered as the Qin at confidence 1.
208 BC: Zhang Chu ends with Chen Sheng's death. The pages do not describe the end of the state as such.

wars.name: Dazexiang uprising (Chen Sheng and Wu Guang uprising)
wars.outcome: The rebels declared Chu at Chen, were beaten back by Zhang Han's Qin forces, and Chen Sheng was killed in January 208 BC.
wars.note: Zhou Wen was ordered west toward Qin proper (Chen Sheng page); the pages give no battle or territory.

sources.title: Chen Sheng
sources.note: King of Rising Chu; capital Chen County; assassinated c. January 208 BC; the break-away of Wu Chen, Zhou Fu and the generals.

sources.title: Chen Sheng and Wu Guang uprising
sources.note: Start August or September 209 BC; Chen declared king of the former Kingdom of Chu; death 4 Jan to 1 Feb 208 BC.

notes: Zhang Chu, Chen Sheng's rebel kingdom, -209..-208 (about half a year; under the ten-year line but flagged by ea-02-a). 2 pages opened (Chen Sheng; Chen Sheng and Wu Guang uprising); both are silent on the territory held, on Wu Guang's siege of Xingyang and on the Zhou Wen march, and neither uses the name 'Zhang Chu' or 'Enlarger of Chu' (they give 'King of Rising Chu', 張楚王). The Dazexiang page's start month is the 7th (9 Aug to 7 Sep 209 BC); the death 4 Jan to 1 Feb 208 BC (the Chen Sheng page: c. January 208 BC). The six rebel kingdoms that broke away (Zhao, Wei, Yan, Qi, Han, Chu) are Cliopatria's rows from -208; the pages opened do not date their founding.
